phase.title: RPC API, real LLM provider, streaming, and demo validation
phase.goal: Expose the finished runtime through a thin RPC-style transport and prove the required end-to-end, cancellation, resume, and failure scenarios.

why_this_phase_exists: Expose the completed application boundary without moving execution logic into transport handlers, then validate the assessment with one real provider and observable JSON execution results.
presentation_follow_up: Phase 4 remains independently demonstrable with its script or commands. The optional phase-4.5-terminal-interface adds an interactive terminal RPC client afterward; it does not move required demo behavior out of Phase 4.
implementation_guidelines: Use FastAPI JSON-RPC over HTTP, Gemini REST via HTTPX and incremental event polling; see implementation_decisions.
Follow docs/requirements/project-brief.md: Keep implementation clean and Retry and cancellation ownership by phase.
Reuse lifecycle, events, serialization, and timeout/cancellation helpers; RPC handlers only validate, delegate, and map results.
Reuse suitable provider SDK facilities or a small existing adapter helper. Share mechanics only when actually common; keep provider error classification inside its adapter.
Use existing async core ports and MCP lifecycle on one asyncio event loop; never call anyio.run per RPC request.
Expose the Phase 3 run supervisor and reuse its storage, task-state and context-selection rules; do not implement a second lifecycle or memory framework.
in_scope: Expose RPC-style operations to create and inspect sessions, submit a message or task, inspect run status, retrieve events, and cancel a run.
Keep endpoint handlers limited to request validation, transport-to-application mapping, stable error mapping, and calls into the application service.
Implement one real LLM provider behind the existing provider interface.
Add bounded provider attempts and request timeouts, connecting real provider cancellation to the Phase 3 lifecycle.
Translate provider tool-call and response formats into core types without leaking SDK objects into the core.
Stream or incrementally poll the persisted Event schema so a caller can observe execution progress, model-step lifecycle, tool calls, tool results, errors, status transitions, and the final answer.
Propagate client cancellation through the application layer to the active run.
Add a documented end-to-end demo using the real provider and separate mock MCP server.
Write the one-page architecture note covering boundaries, trade-offs, limitations, scaling risks, and next steps.
Finalize repository setup and submission instructions.
Wire RPC lifespan to existing application startup/readiness and supervisor shutdown; stop admission and drain/cancel runs before closing shared MCP clients.
Connect the Phase 3 context builder to real provider requests, accounting for instructions, messages, tool schemas and output headroom under a documented input budget.

Add an opt-in, bounded comparison of full-history and selected-context inputs using the same real provider; report correctness, constraint preservation and input size without claiming JSON eliminates lost-in-the-middle errors.
out_of_scope: Automatic fallback or failover to another LLM provider
Claims of production-grade tenancy, exactly-once execution, or unlimited scale
A dedicated Key-Value service, generic JSON state-machine framework, or LLM summarization on every step
Unbounded or automatically executed paid context benchmarks
boundaries_introduced: RPC response envelopes and transport error codes belong only to the RPC adapter, not to AgentLoop or core contracts.
The application service presents transport-neutral session and Run operations to the RPC adapter.
The real provider adapter translates between its SDK and LLMProvider contracts without leaking SDK objects or credentials.
Polling and streaming reuse the same persisted Event schema and sequence ordering.
contracts_introduced: RPC success responses contain ok=true, JSON-serializable data, and a null error.
RPC failure responses contain ok=false, null data, and a structured error with code, message, retryable, and details.
submit_task returns the created Run identity and current status without waiting for terminal completion.
list_run_events accepts an after_sequence cursor and returns ordered events, next_after_sequence, and has_more.
cancel_run is idempotent and returns the latest observable Run state.
get_run returns a lightweight persisted snapshot; complete events remain available through paginated list_run_events, not embedded in every status response.

rpc_operations.behavior: Create and return a durable session.
Return session metadata and documented history summary.
Append user input and start a run without blocking until the full run completes.
Return current structured run state, usage, error and terminal output when available, without embedding the full event history.
Return ordered events with a cursor or sequence offset for incremental inspection.
Record an idempotent cancellation request and return the latest run state.

error.details: JSON object without secrets or stack traces

transport_policy.thin_boundary: RPC handlers must not contain agent-loop, tool-policy, provider, or persistence business logic.
transport_policy.idempotency: cancel_run is idempotent; a generic idempotency framework is out of scope and submit-task idempotency remains optional unless the selected transport requires it.
transport_policy.errors: Map domain errors to stable transport error codes without exposing stack traces or secrets.
transport_policy.streaming: Expose the persisted Event JSON shape; reconnecting clients continue from a supplied per-Run sequence cursor rather than timestamp ordering.
transport_policy.secrets: Load provider credentials from the environment and redact them from logs, errors, events, and fixtures.
transport_policy.lifecycle: RPC lifespan wires shared MCP clients and the Phase 3 run supervisor. Fail startup clearly if required tools are unavailable. Delegate admission, drain/cancel and task cleanup to that supervisor before closing dependencies.

provider_execution_policy.owner: Provider adapter owns retries, with one owner across SDK and wrapper. RPC and AgentLoop add no automatic retries.
retryable_cases: Provider timeout before a usable response is returned.
Temporary connection failure or provider 5xx unavailability.
HTTP 429 only when the provider retry-after guidance fits the remaining run deadline.
non_retryable_cases: Invalid request, unsupported model, or context-limit failure.
Malformed provider response or unknown internal exception.
Cancellation, exhausted deadline, or exhausted attempt budget.
provider_execution_policy.rate_limit: Retry 429 once only with a valid Retry-After or RetryInfo delay that fits the remaining deadline. Without that hint or time budget return PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED. Do not silently switch providers.
provider_execution_policy.fallback: The assessment path uses one real provider and implements no automatic provider fallback. A future explicitly configured provider router is a separate application/infrastructure concern outside AgentLoop.
provider_execution_policy.budget: Use max_attempts=2, including the initial request, so at most one provider retry occurs. max_attempts=1 disables retry. All attempts and waits share the run deadline; retries may incur additional provider usage.
provider_execution_policy.wait: Honor a bounded provider retry-after hint for 429. Use one short fixed delay for other eligible transient failures. Exponential backoff and jitter are future production refinements.
provider_execution_policy.cancellation: Pass remaining time and cancellation through the provider-neutral boundary. Cancel supported local I/O, wake waits, and let Phase 3 reject late output. Distributed worker coordination remains deferred.
provider_execution_policy.trace: Reuse model_request_started and model_response_received with attempt, max_attempts, retry_reason, and retry_delay_ms where applicable. Persist the retry plan before waiting. Usage.model_steps counts logical steps, excluding provider_attempt records; attempts remain independently inspectable.
provider_execution_policy.exhaustion: Return a normalized provider failure after allowed attempts are exhausted. Cancellation and the overall deadline prevent another retry or acceptance of late output.

context_validation_policy.ownership: Reuse Phase 3 selection over core data. The provider adapter owns SDK serialization and provider-specific size accounting; no SQL or provider SDK types enter the context builder.
context_validation_policy.budget: Account for the entire provider request, including instructions and tool definitions, with output headroom. Use supported token counting where available or a documented conservative estimate; never claim an estimate is exact. Reject oversized required context with a stable error before dispatch.
context_validation_policy.evaluation: Keep the real-model comparison opt-in and outside the offline test suite, with explicit request/cost limits. Use the same provider/model/settings and fixtures with relevant facts near the beginning, middle and end of longer histories, distracting material, stale observations and resumed tool exchanges.
context_validation_policy.comparison: Compare full history against the selected-context strategy, both within provider limits. Mark over-budget baselines unsupported instead of silently truncating them. Record task correctness, retained constraints, tool-call validity, input size and observed usage/latency; report regressions and variability, not just shorter prompts.
context_validation_policy.honesty: Record model/configuration, fixture versions, sample counts and whether evaluation actually ran. Missing credentials or an unrun paid evaluation must be reported as not evaluated, not as demonstrated improvement.
context_validation_policy.safety: Task state and tool output remain source-linked data. The model cannot override run status, permissions, cancellation, budgets or unresolved-outcome guards; no new summarization loop or private chain-of-thought capture.

deliverables: End-to-end demo script or documented commands
Architecture writeup of approximately one page
Documented provider input-budget policy and bounded opt-in context comparison with honest execution status

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A caller can create a Session, submit a task, observe ordered execution-progress and tool events without private chain-of-thought, and retrieve the completed result through JSON RPC responses.
A caller can cancel a deliberately slow run and observe a clean persisted cancelled terminal state with no later work scheduled.
The demo includes at least one tool failure, timeout, unknown-tool, or connection-loss case and shows its structured trace.
A session can be resumed after process restart through the public API.
Replacing the RPC transport would not require changes to the agent loop, and replacing the LLM provider would not require changes to core types.
Automated deterministic tests pass without provider credentials; the real-provider smoke test is separate and its execution status is documented.
Provider SDK failures and malformed provider output are returned as stable structured errors without leaking SDK objects, credentials, or stack traces.
Event polling or reconnect continues from an after_sequence cursor and reuses the same Event schema stored by the Harness.
Progress uses fixed templates driven by persisted events, including classified retry reasons and delays; it never infers retry from model prose or exposes private chain-of-thought.

Real provider integration preserves context-selection invariants and rejects required over-budget inputs; the optional real-model comparison reports measured results or explicitly states not evaluated without claiming JSON guarantees better recall.

demo_script: Start the durable runtime and the mock MCP server as separate processes.
Submit a task that requires at least one MCP tool result before the final answer.
Watch ordered events arrive and point out model-step lifecycle, tool-call, tool-result, error, status, and terminal events without exposing private chain-of-thought.
Submit a task that invokes the selected failure fixture and inspect the structured outcome.
Start a deliberately slow task, cancel it through RPC, and show that execution stops cleanly.
Restart the runtime, reload the session, and show the persisted trace or submit a follow-up task.
Explain the transport, core, provider, MCP, and persistence boundaries plus the first scaling bottlenecks.
architecture_writeup_topics: Why the RPC transport is separate from the application and agent core
Why provider SDK and MCP transport types are isolated behind adapters
Execution limits, tool allowlisting, validation, timeout, and retry choices
Persistence, event ordering, cancellation, resume, and interrupted-run semantics
Known limitations and what would change for multiple workers or production load
What would be added with more time and why
Why audit history, runtime authority and compact task context are separate; context-budget tradeoffs and limits of any long-context evaluation
required_tests: RPC contract tests for session, submission, status, events, and cancellation
End-to-end deterministic run through RPC and mock MCP
Event cursor reconnect or incremental polling
Stable transport mapping for validation, not-found, conflict, and internal errors
Provider timeout, unavailability, authentication failure, rate limit, and malformed-response normalization
Transient provider failure then success and exhausted attempts, with ordered events and no hidden SDK retry multiplication
Authentication, invalid-request, malformed-response, and unknown errors do not retry
A short 429 retry-after retries the same provider once; a delay beyond the run deadline returns PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED
No test or production path silently falls back to a second provider
RPC cancel during provider I/O or retry waiting prevents further attempts and late completion
Real-provider smoke test kept outside the default deterministic suite
RPC startup waits for MCP readiness; multiple requests reuse the session; shutdown stops admission and leaves no owned run tasks or MCP processes
RPC delegates to the Phase 3 supervisor and get_run does not return the complete event history
Provider serialization preserves valid resumed tool-call/result groups and distinguishes unknown, cancelled and unexecuted outcomes
Input-budget checks include tool schemas and output headroom; required over-budget context fails without provider dispatch
Offline fixtures preserve task constraints/source references and prevent untrusted task-state data from becoming execution authority

Opt-in real-provider full-history versus selected-context comparison records setup, limits, correctness and input size, including relevant information in the middle; skipped evaluation is explicitly reported
deferred_decisions: Distributed workers, cross-process cancellation, and horizontal scaling
Production observability backend, retention, and tenancy controls

implementation_decisions.transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 over local HTTP POST /rpc using FastAPI; domain operations use the documented ok/data/error envelope inside result, protocol errors use JSON-RPC error. No batch support.
implementation_decisions.provider: Gemini generateContent REST over HTTPX, default gemini-2.5-flash configurable via GEMINI_MODEL; key from GEMINI_API_KEY. One retry owner, no SDK automatic function execution or hidden retries.
implementation_decisions.progress: Incremental event polling at approximately 500 ms; no token-by-token output in this phase. Pure fixed presentation templates map real runtime events and classified errors to status text.
implementation_decisions.cancellation: Explicit cancel_run RPC. A client disconnect is not itself a run-cancel request. Server shutdown drains/cancels before closing MCP, HTTP and storage.
implementation_decisions.continuation: Provider-neutral JSON continuation metadata preserves non-thought response parts and opaque signatures through persistence; never expose these internals via RPC or stream private reasoning.
implementation_decisions.budget: Keep Phase 3 character selection. Before dispatch estimate serialized UTF-8 request bytes plus 1024 overhead, reserve output headroom and reject above the configured combined budget. This is a conservative heuristic, not exact token counting; record observed token usage when returned.
implementation_decisions.api_limits: Local single-worker server, bounded request size and run settings; no production auth/tenancy. Keep RPC read-only status snapshots lightweight and event history paginated.

quality_priorities: Prove cancel during real adapter I/O or retry waiting prevents another model/tool step and late completion; include completion races.
Retain crash-window, outcome_unknown and durable unsafe replay tests; run these regressions alongside RPC tests.
Persist attempt/error/retry plan before sleeping. Errors reported in model prose are not transport failures and do not schedule retries.
Prove real Gemini wire translation with HTTP fixtures, complete resumed tool exchanges, safe error normalization and one attempt owner.
Make setup and success/failure/cancel/restart demos reproducible; keep offline test evidence distinct from live-provider and optional paid evaluation evidence.
exit_condition: All assessment behaviors are demonstrable end to end, checks and setup are reproducible, and the repository contains an honest architecture note with limitations and future work.
